Elemental Urgency: Most Metals Have Inadequate or Nonexistent Alternatives

So wait,the complaint is we dont have substitutes for rare and expensive metals,which are currently used because they are the cheapest available thing that satisfies whatever needed criteria.Wouldnt the substitutes therefore just be even rarer and even more expensive?

Not necessarily. The best illustration is when there was a big panic about a year or two ago over the availability of the rare earths. The main supplier was China, but behind that situation was a history of where China deliberately undercut other suppliers so as to achieve almost monopoly status in supplying the materials. Then China tightened the screws for political reasons. This set off a big (almost) panic, and alternative sources were looked at intensely. One was a disused site in the USA if memory serves me well. I'm afraid I don't know the present status of the elements in question, but the incident was instructive. The point is that neither 'cost' nor 'usefulness/efficiency' can be looked at in isolation from other factors, many of them geopolitical. The 'free market' in materials such as these is often very complicated due to such other factors.
